text:
This looks like May 2019. The fed funds rate is 2.39%, which matches the 2.38–2.40% range of early-to-mid 2019. Unemployment is 3.6%, which was reached in April and May 2019. The 10-year yield at 2.22% fits end of May 2019 (it was about 2.14%), and the 2-year at 2.06% fits too (about 1.95% at end of May).

US large-cap equity fell 5.7% in the month, which matches May 2019 (S&P down about 6.4% in the month). Long Treasuries rose 6.4% in the month, also consistent with May 2019. Headline CPI at 2.0% and core at 2.07% fit April 2019 data, which was the latest available at end of May. Payrolls averaging 169k fits too.

The 10y–2y spread of 0.16 is a little off, but the other cues fit May 2019 well.
